text.p: These were the main headlines from Lithuania's M-1 plus radio station's news report on Monday at noon. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The International Monetary fund decided to distribute to Lithuania another $30 million loan. The decision was passed at the June 26 meeting of the IMF board of directors meeting.

The decision was based on the results of the IMF mission to Lithuania at the end of April and the beginning of May. This will be the last loan according to the economic policy memorandum that was signed in 1994.

In three years, the IMF has given Lithuania $200 million worth of loans. Half of the latest loan will be used for the stabilisation of the national currency and the other half for the needs of the government.

- Parliament is expected to pass a law this afternoon on the legal status of people who suffered during the Soviet occupation. Parliament will also decide whether to create a commission to deal with issues related to Ignalina nuclear power plant.

- The Liberal Union won yesterday's elections in the Shvenchioniu region for the local government board. The party will have 10 seats. The second-place Womens' Party and Homeland Union (Conservatives) gained three seats each.
